scenes.heading: HTL Block Statements
scenes.narration: Components. HTL Block Statements. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What are HTL block statements?
scenes.heading: data-sly attributes on HTML elements
scenes.body: The block statements section begins by defining block statements as data-sly attributes on HTML elements.
scenes.narration: What are HTL block statements? data-sly attributes on HTML elements. The block statements section begins by defining block statements as data-sly attributes on HTML elements.

scenes.question: What is data-sly-use for?
scenes.heading: Initializing a helper object such as a Sling Model
scenes.body: The speech says data-sly-use initializes a helper object such as a Sling Model.
scenes.narration: What is data-sly-use for? Initializing a helper object such as a Sling Model. The speech says data-sly-use initializes a helper object such as a Sling Model.

scenes.question: What is the difference between data-sly-list and data-sly-repeat?
scenes.heading: data-sly-list keeps the host element and iterates over its content, while data-sly-repeat repeats the host element itself
scenes.body: The block statements section explicitly contrasts them: data-sly-list keeps the host element and iterates over its content, while data-sly-repeat repeats the host element itself.

scenes.question: What identifiers does data-sly-list expose by default?
scenes.heading: item and itemList
scenes.body: The speech says data-sly-list exposes an item and itemList by default.
scenes.narration: What identifiers does data-sly-list expose by default? item and itemList. The speech says data-sly-list exposes an item and itemList by default.

scenes.question: What information does itemList provide in a data-sly-list loop?
scenes.heading: index, count, first, middle, last, odd, and even
scenes.body: The block statements section lists the itemList properties as index, count, first, middle, last, odd, and even.

scenes.question: What useful pattern does data-sly-test support besides conditional rendering?
scenes.heading: It can store its result in a variable that can be reused later and is not scoped to the element
scenes.body: The speech gives the example data-sly-test.hasTitle="${properties.jcr:title}" and explains that the result can be stored in a variable, reused later, and is not scoped to the element.

scenes.question: Given a scenario where data-sly-test and data-sly-list are on the same element, when is the test evaluated?
scenes.heading: It is evaluated once before the loop starts
scenes.body: The speech explains that list runs after test in the priority order, so a data-sly-test on the same element as data-sly-list is evaluated once before the loop starts.
